fieldMarks: Yellowish-brown to rufous coat profusely dappled with white spots year-round
White abdomen, rump, throat, inner legs and underside of tail; dark stripe from nape nearly to tail tip
Males carry three-tined antlers; the brow tine forms nearly a right angle with the beam
Females smaller and usually antlerless; males 30–75 kg
behavior: Gregarious; herds range from a few animals to over 100, usually led by an old doe
Adult males normally live in mixed herds, unlike native deer
Rutting males give bugle-like bellows; both sexes bark in alarm
Bucks in hard antler and rut can be found in any month; main breeding mid-May to August, most Texas fawns born January to mid-April
habitat: Secondary forest broken by grassy glades with water and shade; avoids rugged terrain; grazes short green grass and sedges, supplemented by browse.
range: Native to India, Nepal and Sri Lanka. Introduced into Texas about 1932, where more than 15,000 are free-living in central and southern counties; also established in Hawaii and Florida.
